slides.title: Overview of Sentinel-2
slides.text:
- Launched as part of the European Commission’s Copernicus program on June 23, 2015
- Multispectral Instrument (MSI)
- Wide-swath, high-resolution (10 to 60m)
- Support Copernicus Land Monitoring studies, including the monitoring of vegetation, soil and water cover, as well as observation of inland waterways and coastal areas
- Two products:
- Level 1-C
- Level 2A  (Cloud Score+  can be applied to either L1C or L2A collections)

Creating Mosaics and Composites

slides.title: Overview of Sentinel-2
slides.text:
- Orbital Characteristics
  - Altitude: 786 km.
  - Inclination: 98.62 deg
  - Period: 100.6 min
  - Cycle: 10 days
  - Type: Sun synchronous (Near-polar)
- Swath Width: 290 km
- Mean Local Solar Time (MLST) at the descending node is 10:30 (am).
- Launch Mass: 1140 kg
- Design life: 7 years (Nominal Mission) to 12 years (Maximum)

slides.title: Image Pre-processing
slides.text:
Atmospheric Correction

Removes the effects of atmospheric particles (like dust, water vapor) to retrieve true surface reflectance from satellite imagery

Radiometric Correction

Adjusts sensor errors and inconsistencies in image brightness to ensure the pixel values accurately reflect surface energy.

Topographic Correction

Reduces illumination differences caused by terrain (e.g., slopes and shadows) to improve spectral consistency across varied topography.

- BRDF Correction (Radiometric correction): brdf_module
- Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function
- Function of incidence and reflection of the light from a terrain surface by means of a physical model
- BRDF plays an important role in the radiometric correction of satellite images

Create Topography correction module (topographic_module)

- Topographic illumination correction (terrain correction) : to observe geophysical values to remove the effects of topography in mountain areas.
- Illumination conditions vary depending on sun position, slope and aspect and might occur signal to noise ratio
- Adjusting differences in solar irradiance related to slope and aspect (topographic correction) can be used to reduce
- Use Digital Elevation Model
- First, calculate illumination condition (provided by Patrik Burns and Matt Macander)
- Create illumination_Correction function
